alsoPublished.reason: The reader concluded this page gives nothing for the service dimension. It is wrong, and the page says so in a sentence of its own: 'The following table lists AWS services that are integrated with AWS KMS and support the use of the kms:ViaService condition key in customer managed keys'. The table that follows has a 'Service name' and an 'AWS KMS ViaService name' column and 92 rows, e.g. '| Amazon AI Operations | aiops.{{AWS_region}}.amazonaws.com |'. Every claim carries that row as its quote. The reader most likely lost the table, which the Markdown twin renders inconsistently and which we recover from the HTML.

coverageDimensions:
SERVICE coverage would mean: which AWS services can appear as a value of kms:ViaService, kms:GranteeServicePrincipal, or kms:RetiringServicePrincipal - that is, which AWS services integrate with KMS. THE PAGE GIVES YOU NOTHING. kms:ViaService names AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon EBS only as prose examples and shows one endpoint string (ec2.us-west-2.amazonaws.com); kms:GranteeServicePrincipal and kms:RetiringServicePrincipal use the literal placeholders service-name.amazonaws.com and {{service-name}}.amazonaws.com; kms:GrantIsForAWSResource links out to aws.amazon.com/kms/features/#aws-service-integration for the list. Three prose examples are not an enumeration and must not become a service list.

REGION coverage would mean: in which AWS Regions these condition keys are available. THE PAGE GIVES YOU NOTHING. It contains exactly four Region strings - us-west-2, us-east-1, ap-southeast-2, eu-west-3 - every one of them inside an example ARN, an example endpoint, or an example kms:ReplicaRegion value list. kms:ReplicaRegion explicitly hands the Region list off: "For a list of the names of AWS Regions that AWS KMS supports, see AWS Key Management Service endpoints and quotas in the AWS General Reference." Region availability of the condition keys themselves is never stated.

RESOURCE TYPE coverage would mean: which AWS resource types these conditions can be attached to or evaluated against. THE PAGE GIVES YOU ALMOST NOTHING - one resource type, the KMS key. The page repeatedly defines a "KMS key resource operation" as one showing "KMS key" in the Resources column, and points at the Actions and Resources Table on a different page for that mapping. Custom key stores, aliases and grants appear as KMS sub-objects in operation categories, not as an enumerated resource-type list. There is no resource-type list to harvest here.

features.reasoning: The page's own unit of documentation is the condition key: one H2, one anchor, one table, one description each. The values are names AWS KMS publishes about itself, so this is a catalogue, not an external universe - KMS holds 100% of its own condition keys by definition and a percentage over this list is meaningless. It is still worth recording as an inventory, and the Policy type column carries a real, non-trivial exclusion.
features.scope: Two stated per key, both in the per-key table: Policy type ("Key policies and IAM policies" vs "IAM policies only") and API operations (which KMS operations the key controls). Four keys state a different policy type per operation row, so the real cell is (condition key x operation) -> policy type.
features.statuses: All 38 are stated as provided and supported. 0 are stated as retired, removed, or unsupported. 2 are headed "(deprecated)" - kms:CustomerMasterKeySpec and kms:CustomerMasterKeyUsage - but the page explicitly says "to avoid breaking changes, AWS KMS supports both condition keys", so deprecated here means superseded-but-live, NOT not-covered; these 2 are also the only sections with no table. The only genuine Yes/No column is Policy type: 2 keys are "IAM policies only" (kms:ResourceAliases, kms:TrailingDaysWithoutKeyUsage) and so cannot be used in key policies; 4 split by operation (kms:BypassPolicyLockoutSafetyCheck = IAM only for CreateKey, both for PutKeyPolicy; kms:KeyOrigin, kms:KeySpec, kms:KeyUsage = IAM only for CreateKey, both for KMS key resource operations); the remaining 30 with tables say both (kms:GranteePrincipal words it "IAM and key policies" - same meaning, different wording). Secondary attribute counts: 3 keys are Multi-valued (kms:EncryptionContextKeys, kms:GrantOperations, kms:ResourceAliases), 33 Single-valued, 2 unstated.

features.featureName: API operations controlled by AWS KMS condition keys
features.reasoning: "Condition key X controls operation Y" is coverage-shaped and the set is enumerable, so it is a second, separate list from the key catalogue. It is still a catalogue axis - these are KMS's own API operations, not an external universe - and it must be recorded as partial, because the page names 25 but defers three whole categories to another page. Any denominator built from this page alone would be wrong.
features.scope: Per condition key - this is the API operations column of the same 36 tables, read as a matrix of (condition key -> operations).
features.statuses: 25 distinct KMS API operations are named by name across the tables: CreateKey, PutKeyPolicy, Encrypt, Decrypt, ReEncrypt, GenerateDataKey, GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext, GenerateDataKeyPair, GenerateDataKeyPairWithoutPlaintext, CreateGrant, ListGrants, RevokeGrant, RetireGrant, ImportKeyMaterial, DeriveSharedSecret, GenerateMac, VerifyMac, Sign, Verify, DescribeKey, GetPublicKey, ReplicateKey, UpdatePrimaryRegion, EnableKeyRotation, ScheduleKeyDeletion. The axis is deliberately INCOMPLETE on this page: 3 table cells give an unenumerated category instead of operations - "KMS key resource operations" (used by 9 keys), "Custom key store operations" (kms:CallerAccount), and a link to "Cryptographic operations" (kms:RequestAlias) - and the page sends you to the Actions and Resources Table on kms-api-permissions-reference for the membership of the first. Two explicit negatives: ListKeys is called out as an operation where KMS-key resource conditions "can never be satisfied", and GenerateRandom is called out as unaffected by kms:RequestAlias. Two "no effect" carve-outs limit scope rather than operations (kms:EncryptionAlgorithm and kms:SigningAlgorithm have no effect on work done outside AWS KMS with a public key; kms:EncryptionAlgorithm has no effect on the four GenerateDataKey* operations because they always use a symmetric algorithm).

shouldNotExtract: The 38-item Topics bullet block at the top (navigation - it duplicates the H2 sections; counting both double-counts the catalogue). The 30+ "See also" bullet lists that close most sections (cross-links between condition keys, not coverage). The whole "Using set operators with condition keys" explainer, the single-valued vs multi-valued definitions, the ForAnyValue/ForAllValues explanation and the OverlyPermissiveCondition warning text. Every example JSON policy document - and everything inside them: account id 111122223333, principals and role names (ExampleRole, RoleForExampleApp, Administrator), Region strings, IAM action strings (kms:ReEncrypt*, kms:GenerateDataKey*, kms:CancelKeyDeletion, kms:Decrypt), Sid strings, and grant operation values (Encrypt, Decrypt, ReEncryptTo, ReEncryptFrom). The kms:EncryptionContext sub-topics on multiple pairs, case sensitivity and IAM policy variables (~350 lines of usage guidance, zero enumerable values). Enum values quoted in prose as valid parameter values - AWS_KMS / AWS_CLOUDHSM / EXTERNAL_KEY_STORE / EXTERNAL, PRIMARY / REPLICA, RSA_2048 / RSA_3072 / RSA_4096 / SM2, RSAES_OAEP_SHA_1 / RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256 / SM2PKE - these are parameter domains, not coverage. All outbound links to the IAM User Guide, KMS API Reference and AWS General Reference, including the endpoints-and-quotas link. Note: this page carries no AI-coding-assistant boilerplate bullet - I checked the page foot.
trap:
Manufacturing Region and service coverage out of example JSON. A careless parser scrapes us-west-2, us-east-1, ap-southeast-2 and eu-west-3 out of example ARNs and a kms:ReplicaRegion value list and reports "AWS KMS condition keys: 4 Regions supported", and scrapes Lambda / DynamoDB / EBS out of one prose sentence and reports "3 services". Both numbers are fabrications: the page states no Region availability at all and explicitly redirects the Region list to the AWS General Reference and the service list to the KMS features page.

The other four mistakes, in order of likelihood: (1) marking kms:CustomerMasterKeySpec and kms:CustomerMasterKeyUsage as NOT covered because their headings say "(deprecated)" - the page says outright that AWS KMS supports both, so they are supported-and-superseded, and their missing table means missing data, not a No; (2) counting the Topics block plus the H2 sections and reporting 76 condition keys; (3) treating the strings "KMS key resource operations", "Custom key store operations" and "Cryptographic operations" as literal API operation names instead of unenumerated categories that this page deliberately does not expand, which both invents three fake operations and silently understates the true operation count; (4) publishing a percentage over the condition-key list - 38/38 is 100% by construction, because it is KMS's own catalogue, and printing that as a coverage score is meaningless.
whatThePageStates: This is a policy-authoring reference. It enumerates the AWS KMS-specific IAM/key-policy condition keys and, for each one, gives a five-column table (AWS KMS condition keys | Condition type | Value type | API operations | Policy type) followed by prose and example policy statements. The enumeration is the 38 H2 sections, each anchored (kms:BypassPolicyLockoutSafetyCheck through kms:WrappingKeySpec); the identical 38-item Topics bullet list at the top is only navigation for those sections. The page also carries a general explainer on single-valued vs multi-valued keys and the ForAnyValue/ForAllValues set operators, which enumerates nothing.
